summary: Gateway heartbeat drift causing accept-queue buildup and upstream worker crashloop / elevated server error rate
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 16:20 UTC we observed a sustained rise in 5xx responses from the customer's tenant (NimbleChat) affecting chat generation routes. Error rate rose from baseline ~0.4% to ~8% over 30 minutes. Customer reported degraded chat UX and intermittent failures for streaming sessions. Impact: Production traffic for NimbleChat experienced elevated error rates and increased tail latency; several in-flight streaming connections were terminated and retried, amplifying load. Environment: Production (us-east) - shared hosted API; tenant on mixed-embed/chat routes.
timeline:
2026-03-13 16:10 UTC - NimbleChat reported slow responses via support channel
2026-03-13 16:15 UTC - SRE alert: gateway hb_miss_rate spiking; accept_queue depth rising on several frontends
2026-03-13 16:18 UTC - Error rate crosses P1 threshold (>=5% for 5m) for tenant route /v1/chat/stream
2026-03-13 16:25 UTC - Observed upstream runtime worker process crashloop (rapid restarts every ~12s) correlated with GPU watchlog entries
2026-03-13 16:32 UTC - Mitigation applied: increased gateway accept_queue limit and temporarily disabled aggressive health-probe backoff
2026-03-13 16:45 UTC - Error rate reduced to ~1.2% and streaming failures rate returned closer to baseline
2026-03-14 09:00 UTC - Task created to roll a runtime patch and extend telemetry retention for postmortem
investigation_notes: Hypotheses considered: (A) L7 proxy health ping scheduling drift caused head-of-line blocking in accept queues, (B) slow/misordered keepalive handling in legacy proxy revision, (C) a regression in runtime preemption/worker lifecycle handling aggravated by accept-queue backlog. Evidence found: - proxy metric hb_miss_rate increased from ~0.01 to 0.6 (16:15->16:25) while accept_queue_depth for frontends jumped from <10 to >120. - tracing shows gateway spent >1s in accept path before proxy handed socket to upstream worker at 16:22. - runtime logs show repeated worker restart traces with SIGABRT and a note in driver logs about temporary GPU context loss at 16:24 (short, recoverable). - No mass OOM on host; restarts appear triggered by watchdog due to stalled handshake and prolonged socket hold. Cross-checks: unrelated NVMe snapshots occurred earlier in the cluster but not co-located with impacted frontends. Correlation stronger with proxy heartbeat timing and backlog.
mitigation: Temporary mitigations applied 2026-03-13 16:32 UTC: - Increased accept_queue_max for impacted gateway pool from 128 -> 1024 to reduce immediate head-of-line failures. - Reverted recent proxy optimization that reduced healthcheck concurrency. - Adjusted healthcheck interval back to 2s (from 500ms experimental). These reduced retry amplification and lowered instantaneous load on runtimes. Customer was advised to throttle concurrent streaming sessions and disable aggressive client-side retry for 30m.
resolution: Partial resolution in-flight: mitigations reduced error rate and stabilized streaming connections. Engineering has identified a bug in the proxy's delayed-healthcheck path that can leave socket handoff delayed and cause upstream watchdog timeouts under accept-queue pressure. A runtime guard PR (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2487) was opened to ensure slow handoff does not count toward worker watchdog threshold. Full rollout plan: - Patch proxy library to fix scheduling drift (canary 2026-03-15) - Roll runtime guard alongside patch - Monitor hb_miss_rate, accept_queue_depth, and customer error rate for 48h after rollout.
next_steps:
1) SRE: schedule proxy library canary 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC (Ethan)
2) Runtime team: merge and canary PR #2487, ensure graceful backoff when accept queue high (Priya)
3) DX/Support: follow up with NimbleChat with timeline and ask for traffic window to confirm full resolution (Maya)
4) Postmortem doc and RCA to be created under confluence/runbooks within 72h
5) Add automated alert to detect hb_miss_rate > 0.1 for >3m for any single tenant
